explain.say: In the evaporator, a liquid refrigerant at low pressure boils even below freezing. Boiling needs heat, so it soaks heat out of its surroundings and makes them colder.

faq.a: Cold, low-pressure liquid refrigerant boils into a gas. Changing from liquid to gas takes in a lot of heat, so the evaporator cools whatever is around it.
asks: Why does a refrigerant boil at low temperatures?

faq.q: Why does the compressor make the gas hot?
faq.a: Squeezing a gas into a smaller space packs the energy of its particles together, raising its temperature, the way a bike pump gets warm.
asks: What does the compressor do in a fridge?

faq.a: The hot, high-pressure gas flows through a coil, gives its heat to the cooler air around it and condenses back into a liquid.
asks: Where does the heat go in the refrigeration cycle?

faq.q: What does the expansion valve do?
faq.a: It is a narrow opening. When the high-pressure liquid passes through, its pressure falls, part of it boils, and the rest becomes very cold.

faq.q: How can a machine move heat from cold to hot?
faq.a: Heat does not flow from cold to hot on its own, so the cycle needs energy, which the compressor supplies. The refrigerant is used like a sponge, soaking up heat in one place and squeezed out in another.
asks: Does a fridge break the laws of physics?

facts: Many household fridges use the refrigerant isobutane, which boils at about minus 12 °C at normal air pressure.
A refrigeration cycle needs an energy input, usually an electric compressor, to move heat from cold to warm.
